conflicts.fact: Number of chambers in the fish heart and how fish blood is oxygenated/circulated
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 describes a 'two-chambered heart' but also lists four labelled parts (sinus venosus, atrium, ventricle, conus arteriosus); this is consistent with two main chambers. Lesson 4 also says blood passes through 'TWO sets of capillaries' and calls the single circuit 'more efficient than an insect's' system. That is not a contradiction with other lessons, but Lesson 5's efficiency meter ranks fish ~80% above frog ~65%, lizard ~75% and grasshopper ~60%, whereas Lesson 5 teaches that reptiles and amphibians mix blood and Lesson 1 says it is not about 'better' animals.

conflicts.fact: Heart progression used in Lesson 6 prediction vs. content of earlier lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says learners have 'seen the hearts of a grasshopper, a tilapia, and a frog' and the wall chart shows 'open vessel, two chambers, three chambers', omitting the reptile heart that Lesson 5 covered.

conflicts.fact: Kipchoge's heart rate recovery time and the heart rate from which he recovers
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 data sheet: 172 to 38 bpm in about 4 minutes, narration says under 100 bpm within 90 seconds, and the anchoring phenomenon says 'over 170' to approx 37 resting. Lesson 7 says 172 to 37 in under 4 minutes. Lesson 1 curve gives 38 bpm as the endpoint while elsewhere resting is 37. Minor numeric variation.

conflicts.fact: Whether the grasshopper has a heart and whether Kipchoge's SAN/heart rate reasoning is consistent; the nature of the tilapia/frog circulation and the 'double circulation' of fish
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says the dorsal vessel is a pump with 'no chambers like a human heart'. Lesson 12 says the grasshopper has 'no heart chambers — just a tubular pump'. Lesson 1 and 6 refer to the grasshopper having 'no proper heart' and Lesson 6 progression chart calls it 'open vessel'. Lesson 4 says the fish system sits 'between' these. Lesson 12 groups frog with fish under 'closed systems' while Lesson 4 says the fish system is CLOSED and single. These agree overall, so only wording differs.

conflicts.fact: Resting heart rate used in cardiac cycle calculation vs Kipchoge's resting rate and untrained stroke volume
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 Explain phase uses 0.8 s per beat = 75 BPM at rest as the standard, while Lesson 7 also states an average untrained heart has stroke volume about 67 mL, implying about 70-75 BPM; consistent. However Lesson 6 says a sheep heart beats about 70 to 80 per minute, and says Kipchoge's heart is 'the same size' as the sheep's, which is not a conflict with other lessons.

conflicts.fact: Lesson references for evidence cited in the final presentation
conflicts.versions: Lesson 12 sample sentence says pulse rate was measured in Lesson 4, the heart diagram studied in Lesson 7, and circulatory diagrams for grasshopper/tilapia/frog/human compared in Lesson 9. In the sequence, pulse rate was measured in Lessons 2 and 7, the heart diagram in Lesson 6, and the comparison of circulatory systems in Lesson 11 (Lesson 4 is the tilapia diagram, Lesson 9 is immunity/clotting).

conflicts.fact: Lesson in which the cumulative model began
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1-9 and 12 say the cumulative model began in Lesson 1; Lesson 10 says it was 'begun in Lesson 7 and revised in Lessons 8 and 9'; Lesson 11 says it has been built 'since lesson 3'.

conflicts.fact: Where lessons say the Lesson 1 model starts and what it showed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: learners sketch a generic transport system model (heart, arrows or a tube). Lesson 3 says 'In Lesson 1, they sketched Kipchoge's human circulatory system' and that Lesson 2 'added baseline exercise data'. Lesson 9 says the model 'began as a simple outline of Kipchoge crossing the finish line'.

conflicts.fact: Heart rate/phenomenon dataset: Berlin marathon year
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 data sheet labels Curve A 'Berlin 2022' and narration offers 2018 or 2022; Lesson 7 says Berlin Marathon with no year; Lesson 10 says Nairobi Marathon. Minor.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in sub-strand and DQB timing
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 refers to 'twelve lessons'; Lesson 6 says the DQB progression covered 'six lessons' and a grasshopper question was posted 'three lessons ago' (Lesson 3 -> Lesson 6 is consistent). Lesson 1 says the grasshopper-heart question is answered in 'Lesson 3', consistent.

conflicts.fact: Whether the lymphatic system/plasma compartment concept conflicts with how Lesson 8 states pressure drives fluid loss in Kipchoge's capillaries vs. Lesson 4 teaching pressure
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 teaches blood passes through TWO sets of capillaries in fish causing pressure drop, while Lesson 8 says oedema is prevented by lymph draining fluid. These do not contradict each other.

conflicts.fact: Cardiac output figure / 20+ litres per minute vs stroke volume values
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7: Kipchoge's stroke volume about 135 mL, with 'normal cardiac output at only 37 BPM' (37 x 135 = about 5 L/min). Lesson 12: delivers '20+ litres of oxygenated blood per minute' under race conditions; at 170 bpm x 135 mL = about 23 L, so this is consistent.
Lesson 5 uses the Nile monitor lizard heart and lizard at 75% efficiency; Lesson 11 requires a reptile row but gives no example, no conflict.

Lesson 4 asks learners to draw the fish heart 'to scale relative to the four-chambered mammalian heart already on the model', but the four-chambered mammalian heart is not added to the model until Lesson 6; Lesson 11 asks for five hearts to scale.

conflicts.fact: Frog heart blood mixing and efficiency percentage ordering across animals
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 efficiency meter: Grasshopper ~60%, Fish ~80%, Frog ~65%, Lizard ~75%. Lesson 5 also says the grasshopper's haemolymph does not carry oxygen at all (Lesson 3), so a '~60% oxygen delivery efficiency' for the grasshopper contradicts Lesson 3's statement that haemolymph carries no oxygen.
